gap: No result ChatGPT got states the gain arithmetic behind its 'MM phono' label for the Rega Elex MK4. Rega's MK4 phono stage is moving-magnet only, and Rega sells a separate 'Dedicated Moving Coil phono stage' (Fono MC) to go with it. A moving-coil cartridge needs about 20 dB (10×) more phono gain than a moving-magnet one: Musical Fidelity gives its A1 40 dB for MM and 60 dB for MC, rated at 5 mV MM and 450 µV MC. So the Rega is the only pick on ChatGPT's list that cannot properly drive a low-output MC cartridge without buying another box.
standout_why: ChatGPT's own answer already labels the Rega 'MM phono' and the others 'MM/MC', so part of this is already on screen. What it never says is that an MC cartridge needs a separate MC stage or step-up with the Rega, why that is (MC output is about a tenth of MM, so about 20 dB more gain is needed), or what each amp's MC input expects: Luxman 0.3 mV at 100 Ω, Musical Fidelity A1 1 kΩ at 60 dB. I could not check the cited What Hi-Fi best-list or Rega review: WebFetch returned only the 145-character page title, and curl was not permitted. The cited Stereophile, Rhythm Audio and luxman.com pages I also did not open for this comparison, except luxman.com for the L-505Z specs. So rival overlap beyond ChatGPT's visible answer is unverified.
decides: The cartridge type decides the pick. With an MM cartridge, all five work and the Rega Elex MK4 stays the value choice. With a low-output MC cartridge, the Rega is out unless the shopper adds Rega's separate Fono MC stage (price not sourced). The amps with a real MC input are the Luxman L-505Z (0.3 mV sensitivity, 100 Ω load) and the Musical Fidelity A1 (60 dB gain, 1 kΩ load). The A1 is the cheapest of those on ChatGPT's list ($1,999 as ChatGPT showed it; that price is not checked).

findings.label: Phono stage type
findings.note: Rega's words: 'A high performance Rega designed integrated moving magnet (MM) phono stage is carefully built into the circuit'. The key features say 'High quality moving magnet phono stage'. The page has no moving-coil support and lists the 'Dedicated Moving Coil phono stage' (Fono MC) under Complementary Components.

findings.label: Rated power
findings.value: 72 W per channel into 8 Ω; 90 W into 6 Ω
findings.note: From Rega's spec list. The page also lists a built-in DAC with one optical and one coaxial input, up to 192 kHz / 24-bit.

findings.label: Phono MM input
findings.value: 2.5 mV sensitivity, 47 kΩ, S/N 87 dB or more

findings.label: Phono MC input
findings.value: 0.3 mV sensitivity, 100 Ω input impedance, S/N 70 dB or more
findings.note: Sensitivity is about 8.3 times higher than on MM (2.5 / 0.3), about 18 dB. The page gives no other MC load settings.

findings.label: Rated power
findings.value: 100 W per channel into 8 Ω; 150 W per channel into 4 Ω

findings.label: Phono gain, MM vs MC
findings.value: MM 40 dB (5 mV nominal, 50 kΩ / 100 pF); MC 60 dB (450 µV nominal, 1 kΩ)
findings.note: The MC position adds 20 dB, which is 10× voltage gain. That 20 dB is the shortfall a low-output MC cartridge faces on an MM-only input such as the Rega's. Maker's words: 'Automatic input impedance matching (1K nominal) for MC along with increased gain'. S/N is 75 dB on MM and 70 dB on MC.
